---
title: Hash
description: "Identifier equality without a learned vocabulary."
---

An account's current payment and an earlier payment may share a merchant ID,
even when that ID was not seen during training. `Hash` supplies an equality
signal without learning a lasting vocabulary for the IDs. Here, the application
provides the previous payment's merchant ID alongside the current payment.

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model.xs(
    merchant_id=rf.Hash,
    previous_merchant_id=rf.Hash,
    amount=rf.Number,
    merchant=rf.Category,
    disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True),
)
```

One labeled payment:

```yaml
merchant_id: merchant-8042
previous_merchant_id: merchant-8042
amount: 84.50
merchant: North Market
disputed: false
```

Both IDs identify North Market in this example; the earlier payment must be
known before the current one. The [Category](category.qmd) field separately
lets the model learn persistent patterns for merchant labels seen in training.

## Input and options

Accepts scalar Arrow integers, strings, and binary values. Normalize other
identifier types upstream. A null has its own state.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `n_hashes` | `1` | Positive number of independent signed 64-bit fingerprint lanes. |
| `n_bands` | `8` | Positive lower exponent bound for Fourier features. |
| `offset` | `4` | Positive upper exponent bound for Fourier features. |
| `n_buckets` | `4` | Reconstruction classes per lane; must exceed one. |

## Equality and learning

Every Hash field shares a salt within one local-rank batch. Matching values of
the same Arrow family and matching Hash configuration therefore have the same
representation across fields. Training derives a new salt for every batch
from the run seed, the epoch, and the batch ordinal, so a seeded run encodes
the same batches identically on every repeat; validation, test, and prediction
use zero. Validation uses the same deterministic encoding as inference, so
checkpoint selection is not perturbed by the training salt. Other stochastic
model or masking choices can still affect results. Hashes are not durable
identifiers across library versions.

Hash lanes become Fourier features directly in model space; there is no learned
content vocabulary or projection. Non-valued positions use state embeddings.
Reconstruction predicts quantized hash lanes, with `n_buckets ** n_hashes`
possible fingerprints, rather than recovering the original identifier.

Equal fingerprints provide an equality signal while the tokens remain together.
They do not guarantee a join or item correspondence after branch reduction.
Use `reduction=None` on a transaction-history branch when the root needs its
individual tokens for comparison; see
[Branch reduction](branch.qmd#reduce-branch-memory).

Compare the [unseen-identity equality evidence](../evidence/identity/unseen-identity-equality.html)
with the [sibling-collection overlap boundary](../evidence/relational/direct-sibling-hash-overlap.html).
Their trees show why a working equality representation alone does not establish
successful comparison across collections.
The [retrieval capacity evidence](../evidence/relational/retrieval-capacity.html)
extends this evaluation to distractors, larger collections, and a separately
trained two-hop task, with a separate result for each condition.

## Output

Hash has no decoded public content. `embed=True` can export a contextual
embedding, as described in [shared leaf options](index.qmd#shared-leaf-options).
Keep IDs outside the model schema when equality itself is not useful.
